title: Simple Analogies
source: MindSpark Grade 4 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 6: Simple Analogies
subtopics: Object and its use (pen : writing :: scissors : ?)
Animal and its young (cat : kitten :: dog : ?)
Object and where it is found (fish : water :: bird : ?)
learningGoals: Understand the 'A is to B as C is to D' relationship.
Identify the relationship between the first pair and apply it to the second pair.
Solve analogies from six common relationship types.
coreIdeas: An analogy says: A is related to B in the same way that C is related to D.
First, find the relationship between A and B. Then apply that same relationship to C.
Common relationships: use, young one, part-whole, home/habitat, opposite, number rule.

workedExamples.solution: A pen is used for writing. In the same way, scissors are used for cutting. Answer: Cutting.
A kitten is the young one of a cat. In the same way, a puppy is the young one of a dog. Answer: Puppy.
2 doubled = 4. In the same way, 5 doubled = 10. Answer: 10.

onboarding.coachIntro: Spark the coach opens Simple Analogies with: 'Eye is to See as Ear is to...?' — pausing for the learner to complete it. Then Spark explains the A:B::C:D format and the six relationship types using everyday examples that 9-year-olds recognise.
onboarding.placementRule: Start at Group A for all learners. If two consecutive wrong answers in Groups A–B, spell out the relationship in a sentence before trying the next question.

mission.missionPromise: By the end, you will solve any simple analogy by spotting the relationship and applying it — just like completing a sentence!
mission.successCelebration: Award a badge pulse and coach cheer after every correct group. At lesson end, show 'Analogy Ace' trophy.

microLessonPattern: Coach opens with a relatable pair from daily life.
Coach says the relationship aloud as a sentence: 'A is the ___ of B'.
Student completes the analogy with a word.
Instant feedback repeats the relationship sentence to reinforce.
Review question confirms mastery before next group.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 20 XP per exercise group.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Show streak counter; protect with one free retry before streak breaks.
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Each group unlocks one badge tied to the analogy relationship type.
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Quick coach praise + XP pulse + progress rail tick after every correct answer.

reviewLoop.trigger: Two incorrect attempts triggers a mini-reteach by writing the relationship as a full sentence.
reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Offer a simpler pair with very familiar objects.
reviewLoop.masteryRule: Advance only after a correct answer with the relationship stated.
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Any group with two errors returns at the next session.

beats.teacherLine: Hello, smart thinker! Welcome to Simple Analogies — where you find the hidden connection between words! An analogy is like a matching puzzle. You are told: 'A is to B' — that means A and B are related in some way. Then you are asked: 'C is to ___' — you must find D so that C and D share the SAME type of relationship as A and B. Today we learn six fun relationships: use, young one, part-whole, home, opposite, and number. Let us go!
beats.boardAction: Write 'A : B :: C : D' on the board. Below, list the 6 relationship types with one example each.
beats.expectedStudentResponse: Hear — eyes are used to see, ears are used to hear.
beats.fallbackHint: Eyes help you SEE. What do ears help you do? They help you HEAR! Same relationship: organ : its action.

svgAnimation.text: A : B  ::  C : D   (A relates to B the same way C relates to D)
2. Young one  Cat : Kitten :: Dog : Puppy

beats.teacherLine: Let me show you how I solve an analogy! Question: Cow : Calf :: Horse : ??? Step 1: I say the relationship aloud — 'Calf is the young one of a Cow.' Step 2: Apply the same relationship to Horse — 'The young one of a Horse is a...' FOAL! Answer: Foal. Always say the relationship as a sentence first — that is the secret weapon!
beats.boardAction: Write 'Cow : Calf :: Horse : ?' in the centre. Below: 'Calf = young one of Cow' (circle calf). Then write 'Young one of Horse = FOAL' and circle FOAL.
beats.expectedStudentResponse: Hospital — a teacher works in a school, a doctor works in a hospital.
beats.fallbackHint: A teacher works IN a school. Where does a doctor work? In a hospital! Same relationship: person : their workplace.

svgAnimation.text: Relationship: Calf = young one of Cow

beats.teacherLine: You have the secret weapon — always say the relationship as a sentence first! Work through Groups A to F and complete every analogy. Remember the six types: use, young one, part-whole, home, opposite, number. Let's go!
beats.boardAction: Write the 6 relationship types as a reference: 1.Use 2.Young one 3.Part-whole 4.Home/Habitat 5.Opposite 6.Number rule.
beats.checkpointPrompt: Quick check: what are the two words that go in an analogy format? (A : B :: ___ : ___)
beats.expectedStudentResponse: C and D — C is to D in the same way A is to B.
beats.fallbackHint: The format is A : B :: C : D. You are given A, B, and C. You must find D so the relationship C:D matches the relationship A:B.

svgAnimation.text: Tip: Say the relationship as a SENTENCE first!

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise A: What Is It Used For?
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Find what the first object is USED FOR — then find the same action for the second object!

boardDemo.title: Use Analogy
steps: Relationship: a broom is used to SWEEP
Apply: an eraser is used to... ERASE
boardDemo.teacherLine: Say it as a sentence: 'A broom is used for sweeping. An eraser is used for ___?' Fill in the blank — that is your answer!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Pen : Write :: Knife : ___? What do you use a knife for?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Now you try: Camera : Photograph :: Broom : ___?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Yes! A camera is used to take photographs. A broom is used to sweep. Same relationship!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: say it as a sentence. 'A camera is used for photographing.' Now say: 'A broom is used for ___.' That blank is your answer: sweeping/sweep.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise B: Parent and Baby Animals
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Every animal parent has a special name for its baby. Match the right baby to the right parent!

boardDemo.title: Animal Young Ones
steps: Relationship: Chick is the young one of a Hen
Apply: the young one of a Cow is a... CALF
boardDemo.teacherLine: Learn common animal babies: Hen→Chick, Cow→Calf, Dog→Puppy, Cat→Kitten, Horse→Foal, Lion→Cub, Frog→Tadpole.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Cat : Kitten :: Dog : ___? What is the young one of a dog called?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Wonderful! A cub is the young of a lion. A tadpole is the young of a frog. You know your animal babies!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: a tiny frog that lives in water before it grows legs is called a TADPOLE. That is the young one of a frog — just like a cub is the young one of a lion.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise C: Part of the Whole
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! The first word is a PART of the second word. Find what the third word is a part of!

boardDemo.title: Part-Whole Analogy
steps: Relationship: a wheel is a PART of a car
Apply: a wing is a part of a... BIRD (or Aeroplane)
boardDemo.teacherLine: Ask: 'A wheel is a part of what?' Then ask: 'A wing is a part of what?' Make sure the relationship direction is the same in both pairs.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Page : Book :: Key : ___? A page is part of a book. A key is part of what?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Perfect! A finger is part of a hand. A toe is part of a foot. Brilliant part-whole thinking!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: 'A finger is part of a ___' = hand. Same relationship: 'A toe is part of a ___' = foot. Think of your own body!

sessionFlow.subtopic: Object and where it is found (home/habitat)
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise D: Where Does It Live?
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Every animal or thing has a place where it belongs. Find the home for the second word just like you found it for the first!

boardDemo.title: Home/Habitat Analogy
steps: Relationship: a fish lives in WATER
Apply: a bird lives in... SKY (or tree/nest)
boardDemo.teacherLine: Think of where each living thing naturally lives. Fish→water, Bird→sky, Lion→jungle, Bee→hive, Rabbit→burrow. Each place is the 'home' in the analogy!

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Lion : Jungle :: Bee : ___? Where does a bee live?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Yes! A rabbit lives in a burrow. An ant lives in an anthill. You know animal homes perfectly!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: ants build tunnels underground that form a hill shape — that is their home, called an anthill. Just like a rabbit's home is a burrow.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! Sometimes the relationship is OPPOSITES. Hot is the opposite of Cold — find the opposite of the second word!

boardDemo.title: Opposite Analogy
steps: Relationship: Cold is the OPPOSITE of Hot
Apply: the opposite of Day is... NIGHT
boardDemo.teacherLine: Opposite analogies are the easiest! Just find the opposite word. Hot-Cold, Day-Night, Big-Small, Fast-Slow, Up-Down, Happy-Sad.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Fast : Slow :: Big : ___? What is the opposite of Big?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Exactly! Sad is opposite to Happy. Closed is opposite to Open. You know your opposites!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: when a door is not OPEN, what is it? CLOSED. So the opposite of Open is Closed — just like the opposite of Happy is Sad.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's figure this out together! The numbers are linked by a maths rule — double, half, add 10, square. Find the rule in the first pair and apply it to the second!

boardDemo.title: Number Analogy — Find the Maths Rule
boardDemo.teacherLine: Always find the maths operation between the first pair. Is it ×2 (double)? ÷2 (half)? +10? Square (×itself)? Confirm with the numbers, then apply to the third number.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: 2 : 4 :: 5 : ___? What operation turns 2 into 4? Apply the same to 5.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Your turn: 10 : 5 :: 20 : ___? Find the rule and complete the analogy!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Brilliant! 10 ÷ 2 = 5. Same rule: 20 ÷ 2 = 10. The rule is halving. Number analogy mastered!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: 10 to 5 is getting smaller. 10 ÷ 2 = 5 — the rule is divide by 2 (halve). Apply the same: 20 ÷ 2 = 10.
